name: Found Outdoors
opportunity: Nike already ships the outdoor basketball short it thinks it lacks - the DNA Dri-FIT 6" UV Woven (FN2659), carrying UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-sized zip pocket and a rebound-durability claim, verified live at roughly USD 50 list / USD 45.97 at Rakuten (rakuten.com, checked 3 Sep 2026) - yet three independent research domains wrote outdoor function up as unowned white space (A03-S7, A06-S4, A07-S8). The opportunity is therefore capture, not invention: name and ladder an outdoor franchise off an existing SKU, extend it beyond one 6-inch inseam, price and create it locally for the hot-climate markets that set the competitive price, and make its function legible on a wholesale rack where there is no product copy (A02-S7, A07-S9). The differentiating proof point is a certification, not a fibre: AS 4399:2020 rates UPF on DRY, UNSTRETCHED fabric and requires a label warning that protection may be reduced when wet or stretched (arpansa.gov.au, checked 3 Sep 2026) - so every UPF garment in the category ships with a disclaimer covering exactly the state a basketball player is in. Nike can be the first to certify UPF 50+ wet and stretched, alongside saturated-state dry-time and 20-wash dimensional stability, specified against the 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat a basketball uniform actually traps (A06-S2).
target_consumer: Outdoor and half-court players 15-35 playing on concrete, asphalt and acrylic in hot markets - Greater China lower-tier and rural cities (the CunBA belt, A05-S5), the Philippines, wider Southeast Asia, India, the US Sun Belt, Australia and the Gulf. They play multi-hour unregulated sessions (A06-S3), are soaked inside the first game against a 0.95-1.6 L/h sweat load (A06-S2), have no locker so a phone and keys ride on the body (A06-S4), and increasingly play at dawn and dusk because midday surface temperatures exceed 50C and institutions have formally moved play times (A06-S5). They buy in wholesale doors and marketplaces, not the Nike app (A02-S7), and currently default to Li-Ning Wade UPF 50+ / AT Dry or Anta quick-dry knee-length product at a fraction of Nike's price (A03-S7; Li-Ning Wade shorts listed at RM99.50, approx USD 23, lining.my, checked 3 Sep 2026). A secondary consumer is the coverage-and-storage buyer in the same doors who is not playing outdoors at all but reads the outdoor spec as durability and utility.
consumer_problem_jtbd: 'When I play three or four games outdoors in heat and humidity with nowhere to put my phone, help me stay covered, dry and unencumbered for the whole session - and let me tell, on the rack, which short is actually built for that.' Four failure modes sit underneath it. (1) The garment is specified dry and used wet: UPF, GSM, dry-time and abrasion are all rated on a dry, unstretched swatch while the player is saturated and in deep hip abduction roughly 450 times a game (A06-S2, A06-S1, A06-S7). (2) Storage is appended rather than engineered - open pockets spill, zip pockets are too small for a 6.7-inch phone, and pockets catch fingers mid-play (A06-S4), while Nike's own pocket is simultaneously the headline feature and a reported rip point (A01-S3). (3) Nothing on the rack says outdoor: competitors print function and place on the outside of the garment and Nike speaks tonal-logo minimalism (A07-S9, A03-S7). (4) The consumer's own default has already been solved for him by a domestic brand at a third of the price, so Nike is not entering a vacuum - it is arriving late to a shelf it never contested.
product_idea: A named outdoor franchise built as a ladder off the existing DNA UV Woven block, not a from-zero invention. NAMING DIRECTION: lead with 'Nike DNA Outdoor' so the franchise inherits an existing wholesale-legible name and its shelf space, with the hangtag and leg mark carrying the real story - a COURT RATED spec block reading 'UPF 50+ WET + STRETCHED / AS 4399:2020 + wet-stretch addendum / DRY TIME [x] MIN AT 1.33 KG SATURATION'. An alternative heritage direction is a revived Nike outdoor-basketball name (e.g. Blacktop lineage) which requires trademark and archive clearance before it is proposed. SILHOUETTE: straight-leg woven short, articulated at the hip with a gusseted crotch and a side-seam vent so the hem clears the knee in a low defensive stance rather than only standing (A06-S1). INSEAMS: 7" as the volume hero (the New Balance-proven length, A02-S5), 9" as the coverage/half-court and modesty option (knee-clearing per FIBA/NFHS so it can cross into organised play, A06-S3), and 5" boys'. Deliberately no 11" - that length is the DNA Academy value block and would collapse this franchise's price (A02-S4). FABRIC: 100% recycled-content plain-weave polyester with mechanical stretch, 130-150 gsm, cover-factor engineered rather than chemically UV-treated, because untreated 100% polyester technical sportswear already rates UPF 40-50+ and cover factor is the dominant determinant (Aguilera et al., Photochemistry and Photobiology, 2023, doi 10.1111/php.13679, checked 3 Sep 2026; A06-S7). Abrasion-mapped heavier woven at the seat and outer hip for concrete contact and rebound battles (A07-S8). Perforated laser vent field at the lower leg and back yoke - static venting only; Aerogami is explicitly excluded (A07-S2). CONSTRUCTION: bonded pocket bags with bartacked openings and a reinforced hand-entry (the reported failure point, A01-S3); flat-locked seams tested for 20-wash dimensional stability (A01-S2, A04-S6); a silicone-printed, non-slip drawcord and an internal waist tape specified against slip at saturation (A06-S2). STORAGE: a single low-bounce internal zip pocket at the front-hip, sized to a 6.7-inch phone, hung from the waistband so mass sits at the pelvis not the thigh; two bartacked open side pockets; a key loop; no rear cargo or stamped-wordmark zip pockets, which Jordan already owns (A07-S10). DETAILS: reflective heat-transfer at the hem and back yoke for dawn/dusk play (A06-S5); a linerless build so it layers over the compression short players already wear (A06-S3, A06-S6). COLORWAYS: a four-colour global core (black, deep navy, stone, a high-chroma court colour) plus a city/court graphic capsule using court-line maps and local typography per market - Guangzhou, Manila, Sydney, Phoenix - rather than one exported US graphic (A07-S9, A05-S5, A01-S10).
why_now: Five clocks line up in SS28. (1) Nike's own innovation vector has just landed in basketball: Aero-FIT shipped on the Sabrina 4 collection on 17 July 2026 at USD 75 (nike.com, checked 3 Sep 2026), so cooling is proven in the category and the open question is how fast it trickles into a USD 50-60 outdoor short (A03-S4). (2) The channel has swung: Nike wholesale grew while Nike Digital declined for a tenth consecutive quarter (A02-S7, A04-S1), and a rack-legible outdoor short is a wholesale product, not an app drop. (3) Greater China is a live crisis, not a growth story: Nike GC apparel units fell 8% in FY26 and Q4 FY26 Greater China revenue fell 12% reported / 17% currency-neutral to USD 1.30B (cnbc.com, 30 Jun 2026, checked 3 Sep 2026; A04-S2, A02-S2) - locally created, locally priced product is the stated adidas counter-example. (4) The institutional behaviour change is already documented: Philippine athletic meets moved off the 9am-3pm window from 2024 and Gurgaon court surfaces exceed 50C (A06-S5), which makes an outdoor-specified short a response to a change that has happened, not a forecast. (5) The claim environment tightens: the EU Empowering Consumers Directive applies from 27 September 2026, banning generic and uncertified environmental claims (A03-S5), which rewards a third-party-certified, numeric spec claim and punishes vague function copy - exactly the direction this franchise needs to go anyway.

key_features_benefits.feature: UPF 50+ certified in the WET and STRETCHED state, to AS 4399:2020 plus a published wet/stretch addendum, printed as a numeric spec block on the leg and hangtag
key_features_benefits.benefit: The only sun claim in basketball measured in the state the player is actually in. AS 4399:2020 rates UPF dry and unstretched and requires a label warning that protection may be reduced when wet or stretched (arpansa.gov.au, checked 3 Sep 2026), so every competitor's UPF short ships with a disclaimer covering the whole use case. Peer-reviewed work on 100% polyester sportswear found sweat significantly INCREASED UPF and that more than 75% of 34 fabrics already rated 40-50+ (Aguilera et al., Photochem Photobiol 2023, doi 10.1111/php.13679) - which means the wet claim is likely certifiable at low cost, and the genuinely untested variable is stretch across the thigh in a defensive stance.

key_features_benefits.feature: Saturated-state performance pack: wet weight gain, drip-dry time and drawcord slip specified against 1.33 kg of trapped uniform sweat, plus 20-wash dimensional stability
key_features_benefits.benefit: Converts the one garment-level physiological number in the entire evidence base into testable specs. Basketball uniforms trap 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat, rising with intensity (A06-S2), while the reproducible consumer complaints - seam failure, shrinkage, paper-thin hand after one wash - are all post-wet-state defects (A01-S3, A04-S6). Cheap to test, hard for a value competitor to answer, and it earns the price gap over Li-Ning.

key_features_benefits.feature: Engineered low-bounce storage: one bonded internal zip pocket sized to a 6.7-inch phone hung from the waistband, bartacked open side pockets, key loop - and no rear cargo zip
key_features_benefits.benefit: Answers the unsolved pickup problem directly - open pockets spill, zip pockets are too small for large phones, and pockets catch fingers (A06-S4) - while fixing the specific construction Nike is being reviewed down on, where the pocket is both the headline feature and the reported rip point (A01-S3). Avoiding stamped-wordmark zip cargo also keeps Nike out of the design language Jordan and adidas already own (A07-S10).

key_features_benefits.feature: A 7" / 9" / 5" inseam ladder with a knee-clearing 9", articulated hip and gusset, worn linerless over compression
key_features_benefits.benefit: Serves the two poles the base actually evidences without the 8-inch compromise: 7" for performance, 9" for coverage, modesty and half-court players, both knee-clearing so the garment can cross into FIBA and NFHS play where pickup product normally cannot (A06-S3, A02-S5). The gusset and articulation are specified against ~450 lateral movements and 42-56 jumps per game rather than a standing fit session (A06-S1), and linerless respects that shorts are a top layer over compression at every level (A06-S6).

key_features_benefits.feature: Abrasion-mapped woven at seat and outer hip, plus reflective heat-transfer at hem and back yoke
key_features_benefits.benefit: The two outdoor-specific durability and safety needs nobody in basketball composes into one garment - outdoor function today exists only as scattered features across L.L.Bean, Coolibar, NOCTA and Jordan (A07-S8) - and reflectivity answers the documented shift of play to dawn and dusk in the priority markets (A06-S5). It also transfers the exact consumer logic Nike already validated in China footwear with the S.T. Flare's outdoor durability and traction story (A01-S7).

key_features_benefits.feature: Rack legibility: a printed COURT RATED spec block and hangtag that sell the short with zero product copy
key_features_benefits.benefit: The channel has swung to wholesale where there is no PDP to read (A02-S7), and the competitors winning this shelf print function and place on the outside of the garment - Li-Ning's UPF 50+/AT Dry callouts, BadFive streetball lettering, ballaholic's pocket-first concept (A03-S7, A07-S9). Legibility, not capability, is the measured gap: seven researchers with a live catalogue could not find a Nike SKU that exists.

key_features_benefits.feature: Market-created graphic capsules: court-line maps and local typography per city, on the same certified block
key_features_benefits.benefit: Emerging markets build shorts culture around local identity rather than global specs, and local brands - Ugat, ballaholic, BadFive - own that today (A01-S10, A07-S9, A05-S5). Licensing the certified performance block to local storytelling is cheaper than a new global graphic and is the single move most likely to make the product read native in the CunBA belt and Manila rather than imported.

key_features_benefits.feature: Recycled content held as a compliance baseline, with claim language pre-cleared for EmpCo
key_features_benefits.benefit: Every competitor already claims 70-100% recycled and no consumer feedback cites it as a purchase reason, so it must not lead the hangtag (A03-S5) - but the EU Empowering Consumers Directive applies from 27 September 2026 and bans generic, uncertified environmental claims, which makes the certified numeric spec block the safe and differentiating place to spend hangtag real estate.

target_price.tier: Upper-core performance - above the DNA UV Woven 6" at roughly USD 50, below the DNA 8" at USD 65 that clears at 25% off, and well below the Aero-FIT basketball short at USD 75
target_price.rationale: USD 55 is the only defensible position between two verified anchors. The existing DNA UV Woven 6" lists at about USD 50 and was found at USD 45.97 on Rakuten (rakuten.com, checked 3 Sep 2026), so the certified wet/stretched franchise must sit above it or it cannibalises rather than trades up. The DNA 8" at USD 65 is already clearing at USD 48.75 at Foot Locker (A04-S6), which is the empirical ceiling: a USD 65 outdoor short would land on a shelf that has proven it does not hold USD 65. Nike's apparel growth is price-led with units up only 1% (A03-S9), so ASP must be earned by a new benefit rather than assumed; a third-party certification is the cheapest ASP-accretive benefit available and is the one thing a USD 23 Li-Ning short cannot copy overnight. USD 55 also keeps the franchise under the USD 100 threshold that governs Nike's US price actions (A04-S8) while accepting the audit's correction that the June 2025 freeze was superseded by roughly 3% apparel increases. CRITICAL CAVEAT, per the cross-dataset auditor: no Nike price in the underlying evidence base was anchored to a retrieved page, three mutually incompatible Nike ladders coexist in the file, and the observable clearing band for basketball shorts is USD 29-69. Treat USD 55 as a hypothesis to be tested against internal list-vs-realised ASP and one week of third-party retail price tracking before it is a recommendation.
target_price.regional_notes: GREATER CHINA - the single hardest call, and the base argues both ways inside one signal. Domestic outdoor-claim product sits at RMB 200-300 entry (A01-S7) and Li-Ning Wade UPF product is discounted to roughly EUR 20 from EUR 49 in Europe (A03-S7) and lists at RM99.50 (approx USD 23) at Li-Ning Malaysia (lining.my, checked 3 Sep 2026); yet Nike's own China outdoor precedent, the S.T. Flare, launched at RMB 899 (approx USD 125), which is premium, not value. Recommendation: RMB 279-299 for the 7", created and sourced locally per the adidas proof point (A04-S2), which sits at the top of the domestic value band rather than inside Nike's global translation - explicitly NOT a mid-price average of the two strategies, because they need different products and different margins. PHILIPPINES / SEA - PHP 1,995, which is exactly where Nike DNA basketball shorts already sit at Nike PH and Titan 22 (nike.com/ph and titan22.com, checked 3 Sep 2026), so the franchise creates no new price band and stays inside the sub-PHP 3,000 filter band consumers already shop; A03-S10's call for a sub-PHP 2,000 expression is met exactly. AUSTRALIA - AUD 75-80 through Rebel, JD and Foot Locker AU, where UPF literacy is highest and ARPANSA/AS 4399 is a recognised mark, making it the market where the certification carries the most price (A02-S9, A06-S7). US SUN BELT - USD 55 held at full price through Dick's, Hibbett and Foot Locker; do not enter the promotional cadence in year one, since the marketplace turned increasingly promotional in summer 2026 (A04-S4). EUROPE - EUR 54.99 with EmpCo-cleared claim language from launch (A03-S5).

market_distribution_role: ROLE IN LINE: a named franchise EXTENSION off the existing DNA UV Woven block, not a new franchise from zero and not a seasonal capsule. It is the outdoor pillar of Worldball Innovation and should be planned as a two-season carryover core (four global colours) with a market-created graphic capsule refreshing each season - this is what turns a single 6-inch SKU that nobody can find into a findable, replenishable franchise. It is a hero for SS28 in APLA and Greater China and an entry-to-core proposition in North America. LEAD MARKETS AND SEQUENCE: the base disagrees with the brief here and the disagreement should be surfaced to the Council, not resolved in the deck. SS28 priority points to Greater China, where participation is roughly 300M and Nike has already validated 'built for Chinese outdoor courts' in footwear (A01-S7) - but the branded basketball segment there is contracting and promotional (A02-S3, A04-S2, A02-S2) and no Chinese price or sell-through datum exists anywhere in the base. Australia is the best-evidenced market in the file (roughly 1.3M players, female participation +25% since 2022, NBL attendance 1.09M, an on-court league partner that is not a performance-basketball leader) AND has the highest national UPF literacy and the standard the claim is written against (A02-S9, A06-S7) - which is why OPP-04 argues it should be the proving ground that generates the sell-through dataset. Recommended sequence: Australia and the Philippines as the SS28 proof markets, Greater China as the SS28 scale bet with locally created and locally priced product, US Sun Belt as a Q1 carryover. CHANNEL MIX: wholesale-led, roughly 65/35 wholesale to Nike Direct, inverting the default. Nike wholesale grew while Nike Digital fell for a tenth consecutive quarter (A02-S7) and Nike's own growth is concentrated in wholesale doors (A04-S1). Named doors: Dick's, Foot Locker and Hibbett in the US (all three already merchandise the existing UV Woven SKU); Rebel, JD and Foot Locker in Australia; Titan 22 and Toby's in the Philippines; Tmall, JD, Douyin plus tier-2/3 wholesale in Greater China, where adidas beat Nike in Tmall 618 2026 and domestic e-commerce is growing 35-40% (A04-S11). MARKETPLACES: contest the marketplace shelf directly in SEA (Lazada, Shopee) rather than ceding it to generics (A03-S10). LAUNCH CADENCE: land SS28 in-line at the seasonal reset rather than as a drop; the outdoor season in the lead markets is not the US calendar, so China and SEA should carry a spring-forward flow. A team-dealer expression is explicitly out of scope - that is OPP-01's territory and the pockets make this garment competition-illegal in most organised play anyway (A06-S3).

evidence_stack.contribution: Supplies the entire technical spine and the only garment-level number in the base. A06-S2 (VERIFIED) gives the 0.95-1.6 L/h sweat load and, critically, the 0.00-1.33 kg of sweat trapped in basketball uniforms that the wet-state spec is written against. A06-S7 supplies the UV physics of outdoor courts (concrete reflects 2-15% of UV, tournament days stack 4-6+ hours, sunscreen fails in 40-80 minutes when sweating), the ARPANSA standard, and the observation that Nike's only UPF short is at the shortest inseam. A06-S4 defines the storage problem precisely. A06-S5 supplies the institutional behaviour change - Philippine meet times moved, Gurgaon surfaces above 50C - that makes this a documented change rather than a forecast. A06-S1 and A06-S3 set the fit-test protocol and the rules boundary.

A03-S7 is the competitive core: Li-Ning Wade UPF 50+ / AT Dry, Anta's knee-length quick-dry five-fen, Peak Wending, all at low price points, and the observation that no Nike outdoor short surfaced - which the auditor later turned into the capture finding rather than a white-space finding. A03-S4 (VERIFIED) establishes that cooling is Nike's declared innovation vector and prices Aero-FIT at USD 75, framing the trickle-down question this franchise answers. A03-S9 (VERIFIED) establishes the flat-unit, price-led environment that forces a new benefit rather than an assumed tailwind. A03-S10 supplies the Philippine price bands. A03-S5 keeps recycled content off the hangtag.

A07-S8 catalogues the scattered outdoor ingredients across L.L.Bean's 7-inch UPF 50+ short, Coolibar's Outpace 2.0, NOCTA's water-resistant short and Jordan's 23 Engineered - proving each ingredient is feasible and that none is composed into one basketball design language. A07-S9 (VERIFIED) is the strongest design signal in the stack and drives the graphic and legibility strategy: ballaholic, BadFive and Ugat design around pockets, place and pride while global brands speak tonal minimalism. A07-S10 rules out the zip-cargo 'engineered' language Jordan already owns. A07-S2 is used negatively - it is the reason Aerogami is excluded.

A01-S7 (VERIFIED) is the single strongest strategic precedent in the file: Nike released the S.T. Flare in June 2025 as its first China-only performance basketball shoe, explicitly built for outdoor court durability, traction and heat - proving Nike has already made and validated this exact consumer argument one category over, and never applied it to apparel. A01-S3 supplies the pocket-as-hero-and-failure-point tension that drives the bonded-bag construction spec. A01-S10 grounds the market-created graphic strategy.

A02-S7 (VERIFIED) is decisive for the go-to-market: wholesale grew in Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital fell for a tenth consecutive quarter, which converts rack legibility from a nice-to-have into the primary design constraint. A02-S4 and A02-S5 supply the price ladder and the inseam architecture, both of which the auditor flags as contested. A02-S9 (VERIFIED) supplies the Australia case that makes it the right first proof market. A02-S1 sizes the category at 5-6.5% CAGR with APAC fastest-growing, while warning no source isolates shorts.

A04-S2 (VERIFIED) supplies both the burning platform and the sharpest warning: Nike GC apparel units fell 8% in FY26 against growing participation - a capture failure, not a demand failure - with the adidas +15% Greater China quarter credited to local sourcing and design as the proof of the fix. A04-S1 (VERIFIED) confirms performance basketball is one of Nike's few growth engines and that the bet must be built for wholesale. A04-S6 supplies the empirical price ceiling (DNA 8" clearing at 25% off) and the durability complaint pattern. A04-S8 frames the margin box.

A05-S5 supplies the cultural venue the product is designed from - CunBA village basketball in Guizhou, viral since July 2022 with online viewership above 100 million and spreading to Heilongjiang and Yiwu in 2025 - which is outdoor, lower-tier, authenticity-prizing and served almost entirely by domestic brands today. It is the only culture signal in this stack and it is a PATTERN, not a FACT; it justifies the design brief and the graphic strategy, not the volume forecast.

contradictory_evidence.description: THE WHITE SPACE WAS A SEARCH ARTIFACT. The cross-dataset auditor verified directly across Nike.com, Amazon and Rakuten that the Nike DNA 6" UV Woven (FN2659) already carries UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-sized zip pocket and a rebound-battle durability claim, that nike.com.cn runs a dedicated outdoor section with sun-protection and quick-dry product, and that adidas merchandises standing Outdoor Basketball and Reflective Shorts collections. Three specialists reasoned from the absence of a term in blocked search snippets to the absence of a product in the market, and the same un-run catalogue query was counted three times. Consequence: this is a merchandising, naming and legibility opportunity, and any framing of it as invention is false. It also means the incremental revenue is trade-up and findability, not a new occasion - a materially smaller prize.

THE SUN CLAIM MAY DESCRIBE WHAT THE FABRIC ALREADY DOES, AND THE WET-STATE PREMISE IS PARTLY FALSIFIED. Peer-reviewed testing of 34 100% polyester technical sportswear fabrics found more than 75% already achieve UPF 40-50+ untreated, that cover factor rather than treatment is the dominant determinant, and - contrary to the synthesised thesis - that sweat and moisture SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED UPF values, by over 20% in the biological protection factors (Aguilera et al., Photochemistry and Photobiology, 2023, doi 10.1111/php.13679, checked 3 Sep 2026). The opportunity as originally written assumed wet-state UV protection was an unmeasured risk; the literature suggests it is probably an unclaimed strength. That is not fatal - it makes the certification cheaper and more likely to pass - but it kills the 'nobody knows what happens when it is wet' framing, and it means the marginal value of the claim is marketing legibility, not new physical protection. It also means the genuinely open variable is STRETCH, not moisture: AS 4399:2020 rates dry AND unstretched and warns on both. Additionally, Coolibar already markets 'blocks 98% of UVA/UVB rays - wet or dry' (coolibar.com search result, checked 3 Sep 2026), so the wet claim is unowned only inside basketball, not in apparel.

THE LEAD MARKET IS A CONTRACTING BRANDED SEGMENT. Nike Greater China fell 11-13% in FY26 with apparel units -8%; Q4 FY26 GC revenue fell 12% reported / 17% currency-neutral to USD 1.30B (cnbc.com, 30 Jun 2026); management expects a revenue headwind through FY27; Li-Ning's basketball retail sales fell 19% in 2025 amid deeper discounting; adidas beat Nike in Tmall 618 2026. The auditor's judgement is that the three largest branded players do not aggregate to an 8% growing market and none is growing in basketball - so 'huge participation plus huge growth' is close to the inverse of what company data shows. Worse, the auditor flags an unresolved contradiction inside the counter-case: A02-S3 has Li-Ning basketball down 19% in FY2025 while A04-S2 has it UP 5% in H1 2026 - same company, adjacent periods, opposite direction, and the single most decision-relevant unknown in the China case.

THE PRICE STRATEGY ARGUES BOTH WAYS INSIDE ONE SIGNAL. A01-S7 concludes Nike must land near the domestic RMB 200-300 value band from the same S.T. Flare precedent that launched at RMB 899 (approx USD 125) - premium, not value. The auditor's explicit instruction is not to average these into a mid-price compromise, because a value entry tier and a premium durability story require different products, different margins and different channels. The RMB 279-299 recommendation in this document is a value-tier choice and should be presented to the Council as a choice, not a finding.

NO PRICE IN THE BASE IS ANCHORED TO A RETRIEVED PAGE. The auditor found three mutually incompatible Nike price ladders in the file, none from a retrieved page, in a session where retail hosts were blocked - and warned that some figures may be the search engine echoing query language back. Observable clearing prices for basketball shorts are USD 29-69 while some opportunities in the portfolio price at USD 85-120. The USD 55 in this document is corroborated by two independent live checks (DNA UV Woven at roughly USD 50 list / USD 45.97 Rakuten; DNA PH at PHP 1,995) but remains unvalidated against sell-through. Separately, the inseam architecture is contested: the auditor notes Nike ships a continuous 6/8/10/11-inch ladder with the LONGEST inseam at the LOWEST price (~USD 37), which is the opposite of a premium-short-inseam architecture, and nobody in the base has a single unit of inseam sell-through evidence.

THE PRIMARY USE CASE MAY NOT BE A SUNNY ONE. A06-S5 documents that heat is pushing everyday outdoor play to dawn and dusk in exactly the priority markets - Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Gurgaon, the UAE, the Philippines - which weakens midday UV as the everyday need and shifts weight toward dry-time, low wet cling, low fabric weight and night visibility. UPF then matters mainly for multi-hour weekend tournaments, a narrower occasion than the franchise premise implies. The honest position is that heat management is the corroborated need (PAT-11) and UV is the legible, certifiable expression of it - which is a marketing argument as much as a physiological one.

BASKETBALL IS NOT A HIGH-SWEAT SPORT BY NORMATIVE STANDARDS, AND ALL THE DATA IS INDOOR. Baker et al. 2019 (n=1303) puts basketball's whole-body sweating rate at 0.95 +/- 0.42 L/h - level with soccer and well below American football at 1.51. Designing the line to the 1.4-1.6 L/h competitive tail implies different fabric weight, dry-time and cost targets than designing to the sport mean, and the auditor's verdict is that this is a design choice being presented as a finding. Every measurement is from air-conditioned North American gyms and is overwhelmingly male, yet it is being used to justify hot-humid outdoor Asian and Gulf product.

THE DURABILITY FIX MAY BE AIMED AT THE WRONG DEFECT. This document specifies bonded pocket bags and bartacked openings from A01-S3's ripped-pocket complaint, but the auditor found the better sample points elsewhere: direct retrieval of the same Walmart Icon review corpus surfaces seams failing after one wash, holes across the legs, shrinkage and paper-thin fabric, with the extraction explicitly noting NO ripped-pocket complaints, and Dick's showing Icon+ 6" at 3.9 stars with only 67% recommending across 64 reviews. If seam construction and dimensional stability are the real defect, pocket engineering is an expensive answer to the wrong question - and the competing causal story (that a price freeze forced a fabric cost-down) is correlation dressed as mechanism, since nobody has established GSM changed at all.

THE COOLING PLATFORM QUESTION CUTS BOTH WAYS. Aerogami is deliberately excluded here because three years have produced one Run Division jacket, which the auditor reads as an equally available signal that Nike has already tried and declined to extend it on cost or abrasion-durability grounds. But the same audit entry closes the Aero-FIT gap in the opposite direction: Aero-FIT shipped to basketball on the Sabrina 4 collection on 17 July 2026 - on a WOMEN'S signature short first - so the cooling platform this franchise defers to may arrive in basketball faster and higher up the line than a USD 55 outdoor short can absorb, creating an internal collision rather than a trickle-down. The USD 75 Aero-FIT price could not be confirmed on a retrieved page by the auditor; it reproduces in a search summary (checked 3 Sep 2026) but remains unverified.

CLAIM-SUBSTANTIATION EXPOSURE IN EUROPE. The EU Empowering Consumers Directive applies from 27 September 2026, banning generic and uncertified environmental claims. This franchise's strategy is to put more claims on the hangtag, not fewer. Every spec claim - UPF, dry-time, abrasion, recycled content - needs a legal read and a substantiation file before any European hangtag or PDP copy is written, and no domain in the base addressed claim law at all.

confidence_rationale: 62 reflects a real, multi-domain consumer need attached to a proof point that partly failed its own verification. UPWARD: the need is corroborated by three unrelated evidence pools that share no source - peer-reviewed physiology (A06-S2, VERIFIED), documented institutional behaviour change in the Philippines and India (A06-S5), and a competitor's multi-year commercial platform in Li-Ning's Wade UPF 50+/AT Dry line (A03-S7) - which is the strongest cross-domain corroboration in the portfolio (PAT-11, strength: strong). Nike has already validated this exact consumer argument in footwear with the S.T. Flare (A01-S7, VERIFIED). The channel logic is verified and unambiguous (A02-S7, A04-S1, both VERIFIED). Execution risk is unusually low because the garment substantially exists - this is a naming, laddering, certification and merchandising programme, not an R&D programme. DOWNWARD: the founding white-space claim was an artifact of blocked searches, not a market gap, which shrinks the prize from 'new occasion' to 'trade-up and findability'. The signature proof point was partly falsified by my own check - sweat appears to INCREASE polyester UPF rather than threaten it (Aguilera et al. 2023), so the claim is easier to certify but less physically meaningful than the thesis assumed, and Coolibar already makes a wet/dry claim outside basketball. The lead market named by the SS28 priority space is a contracting, promotional, share-losing segment for Nike, with an unresolved Li-Ning -19%/+5% contradiction at its centre. Not one price in the base is anchored to sell-through, and the inseam architecture is genuinely contested. There is zero sell-through, zero conversion and zero consumer-research evidence anywhere in this file for an outdoor basketball short. 62 is 'commit to a Council-level test-and-learn with a named first market', not 'commit a global SS28 line'.
what_would_need_to_be_true: A live, global SKU-and-feature audit of every Nike basketball bottom must confirm the actual extent of what already ships - inseams, markets, UPF claims, pocket configurations and prices. This one query would have prevented four white-space claims across four domains and it decides whether this is a naming exercise, a laddering exercise, or genuinely both.

The certification must pass in the wet AND STRETCHED state, not just wet. AS 4399:2020 rates dry and unstretched; the literature suggests moisture helps polyester UPF, so the real risk is thigh-stretch in a defensive stance. A test to AS 4399 plus a published wet and biaxially-stretched addendum on three candidate cover factors must return UPF 50+ before the claim is designed into the garment.

USD 55 must hold full-price sell-through for at least two seasons in at least one wholesale door. The DNA 8" already clears at 25% off at USD 65 and the US marketplace turned promotional in summer 2026; if USD 55 discounts in season one, the franchise is a USD 45 product and the certification is a cost, not an ASP driver.

China product must be locally created, locally sourced and locally priced at RMB 279-299 - the adidas mechanism, not a translated US line. If the China expression is a re-coloured global SKU at a global price, A04-S2's unit decline continues regardless of the outdoor story.

Phone-carry behaviour at the court must be quantified. No source in this base measured how many pickup players actually carry a phone on-body, and the storage system is a third of the product's reason to exist. If carry rates in Guangzhou, Manila and Phoenix are below roughly 50%, the pocket architecture is over-engineered.

Wholesale buyers must be able to identify the product's function from the rack in under five seconds with no product copy, in a merchandising test with the four lead retailers. Legibility is the entire capture thesis; if the COURT RATED block does not read at the rack, the franchise fails for the same reason the existing SKU is invisible.

The Aero-FIT basketball roadmap must not collide with this price point. If Aero-FIT scales into a USD 60-65 outdoor-adjacent short inside SS28-SS29, this franchise is squeezed between it and the DNA UV Woven and should be repositioned or merged rather than launched.

The garment must clear the knee in a low defensive stance at both 7" and 9" on the fit block, tested in lateral abduction and at jump-landing hip flexion rather than standing, so the 9" stays FIBA/NFHS-legal on hem length while remaining a pickup product on storage.
what_we_still_dont_know: Whether anyone buys an outdoor basketball short at a premium. There is no sell-through, conversion, search-volume or stated-preference evidence for outdoor-specified basketball shorts anywhere in this base - for Nike, Li-Ning, Anta or anyone. The entire demand case is inferred from participation, physiology and a competitor's assortment decision.

What Li-Ning's Wade UPF short actually sells at, and how much, inside China. Every Li-Ning price in the file comes from a European reseller or a Malaysian site; no retrieved Chinese price exists anywhere in the base, and the RMB 279-299 recommendation is therefore anchored to a foreign proxy.

Whether Li-Ning basketball is recovering or still falling. A02-S3 has -19% for 2025 and A04-S2 has +5% for H1 2026 - same company, adjacent periods, opposite direction, unreconciled. This single number changes whether Nike is entering a recovering or a collapsing branded segment.

What stretch does to UPF in a polyester woven at basketball-specific strain. AS 4399:2020 warns that stretched protection may be reduced and the tested literature covers moisture but not sport-specific biaxial strain. This is the one genuinely open technical question and it is cheap to answer.

Outdoor sweat rates. Every sweat measurement in hand - 0.95 L/h normative, 1.4-1.6 L/h competitive, 0.00-1.33 kg trapped - comes from air-conditioned North American gyms with overwhelmingly male samples, and is being used to specify hot-humid outdoor product for Guangzhou, Manila and Delhi.
How many pickup players carry a phone on-body, and where they want it. Explicitly unquantified in A06-S4.

Which durability defect is real - pocket-area failure, seam failure, or post-wash dimensional change - and whether GSM has actually changed on Icon and DNA between FY23 and FY26. Nike owns this data in warranty and returns codes and nobody pulled it.

Whether the outdoor consumer and the coverage/lifestyle consumer are the same buyer. The 9-inch could be an outdoor performance length or a lifestyle length, and no inseam sell-through split by door type exists in the base.
The SS28 marketing calendar and whether any dated moment - CunBA, a 3x3 circuit, an NBL season - can anchor a launch. Absent from all seven specialist files.
nike_right_to_win: Four assets, one of which is unique and none of which requires new invention. FIRST, Nike has already made and validated this exact consumer argument one category over: the S.T. Flare, released June 2025 as Nike's first China-only performance basketball shoe, explicitly built after studying Chinese outdoor courts for durability, traction and comfort in outdoor conditions (A01-S7, VERIFIED). The apparel companion is the obvious, unbuilt half of a strategy Nike has already committed to and marketed - and no competitor can claim that precedent. SECOND, Nike owns the testing and certification infrastructure to make a wet-and-stretched UPF claim credible at global scale. A value competitor can put UPF 50+ on a hangtag; almost nobody can publish a third-party-certified addendum for a state the governing standard explicitly disclaims, and Nike's sports-research capability is the natural home for a saturated-state garment protocol built on the Baker trapped-sweat method. THIRD, the wholesale shelf where this product must win is where Nike is currently strongest and growing: wholesale grew in both Q4 and full-year FY26 while Nike Digital fell for a tenth consecutive quarter (A02-S7, VERIFIED), and Nike already occupies rack space at Dick's, Foot Locker, Hibbett, Rebel and Titan 22 with the very SKU this franchise extends. Fixing legibility on a shelf you already own is a far cheaper win than buying a new shelf. FOURTH, Nike is one of very few brands able to run a locally-created, locally-priced China expression alongside a global block, which is precisely the mechanism adidas used to grow Greater China 15% in Q2 2026 (A04-S2). THE HONEST LIMIT: Nike has no right to win on price. Li-Ning and Anta own the outdoor vocabulary, the value band and the shelf in the markets with the most outdoor players, at roughly a third of Nike's price (A03-S7). This franchise wins on certified proof, construction and legibility or it does not win - and if the Council is not prepared to fund the certification programme, the correct decision is to merchandise the existing SKU better and spend the money on OPP-03 instead.

narrative: This spec was built by refusing to believe the finding that started it. Four domains independently reported outdoor function as unowned white space, and the cross-dataset auditor showed all four were reading the same blocked search session: Nike ships a DNA 6-inch UV Woven short carrying UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a phone-sized zip pocket and a rebound-durability claim. I re-checked it live and found it at roughly USD 50 list, USD 45.97 at Rakuten, stocked at Dick's, Hibbett, JD Sports and Amazon. So the first judgement call was to write a merchandising opportunity rather than an innovation one, and to accept the smaller prize that comes with it: trade-up and findability, not a new occasion. That reframing is the whole document. It changes the ask from an R&D programme to a naming, laddering, certification and rack-legibility programme - and it changes the risk profile from 'can we build it' to 'will anyone notice'. The second judgement call is the one I argued with myself about longest. The synthesised thesis rested on a beautiful cross-literature insight: uniforms trap up to 1.33 kg of sweat, polyester rates UPF 40-50 dry, therefore the category's sun claim is measured in a state the player is never in. I went to verify it and found the opposite. Aguilera et al. tested 34 100% polyester technical sportswear fabrics and found sweat and moisture SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASED protection factors, by over 20%, with cover factor the dominant determinant. The premise was elegant and partly wrong. I kept the feature and rebuilt its logic. What survives is better and less romantic: AS 4399:2020 rates UPF on dry, unstretched fabric and requires a label warning that protection may be reduced when wet OR STRETCHED - so the whole category ships a disclaimer covering exactly the state a player is in, and the genuinely untested variable is not moisture but thigh strain across roughly 450 lateral movements a game. That is a claim Nike can certify cheaply, print on a leg, and that Li-Ning cannot answer in a season. It is a legibility asset more than a physiological one, and the document says so. I also had to decide against the evidence base's own centre of gravity twice. Once on China: the SS28 priority space points there, but Nike GC apparel units fell 8%, Q4 GC revenue fell 17% currency-neutral, Li-Ning basketball is in a contradiction with itself, and there is not a single retrieved Chinese price anywhere in the file. I did not resolve that - I recommended Australia and the Philippines as SS28 proof markets while keeping China as the scale bet, and flagged the sequencing as OPP-04's argument to have in the room. Once on price: A01-S7 argues RMB 200-300 value from the same S.T. Flare precedent that launched at RMB 899. The auditor forbade averaging. I chose the value tier at RMB 279-299 and labelled it a choice, not a finding. Two features were cut on evidence. Aerogami: three years, one jacket - a feasibility signal, not white space. Rear zip-cargo utility: Jordan owns that language. And one recommendation is knowingly at risk - bonded pocket bags answer a ripped-pocket complaint with a single undated source, while a 64-review sample says the real defect is seams and shrinkage. It is in the spec, and the contradiction is in the document at medium severity, because pulling Nike's own returns codes settles it for almost nothing.
